correctness.rationale: For every n≥5, the two exact closed-neighborhood subcomplexes U,V are separately reduced by explicit relative elementary collapses to (n−2)-spheres; their intersection is exactly the connected 1-dimensional crown graph with n(n−1) edges and 2n vertices. Both inclusion maps are nullhomotopic because the two targets are simply connected, so their simplicial homotopy pushout is U∨V∨Σ(U∩V), yielding integral spheres of multiplicities 2 and n²−3n+1. Every critical collapse has an executable complete free-face check for n≤8; full binary ranks match, but experiments are not used to prove the unrestricted integral statement.

value.rationale: Deleting a perfect matching from the natural baseline K_{n,n} changes the closed-neighborhood complex from a pure wedge of (n−1)² 2-spheres to an explicitly mixed-dimensional wedge with two (n−2)-spheres for all n≥5. This identifies how missing adjacencies create higher-dimensional homotopy, gives exact integral homotopy types for an infinite graph family, and uses an explicit decomposable cover rather than a table reconstruction; the dimension threshold and sharp graph-perturbation comparison have structural motivation.
